title: Lux Radio Theatre
paragraphs: A major dramatic anthology adapting popular motion pictures and stage works for radio, usually with prominent Hollywood actors and often with stars recreating their film roles.

Weekly dramatic anthology sponsored around the Lux brand. The historical series began in New York in 1934 and moved to Hollywood in June 1936, where motion-picture adaptations and major film stars became its defining form. The locked GRH snapshot contains 328 playable recordings from 1936-06-15 through 1955-02-08; the historical radio series continued to 1955-06-07.

GRH documents the program through New York NBC Blue era (October 14, 1934 to June 30, 1935) on [[org|org.acb290b0843b31ec|Blue Network]], New York CBS era (July 1, 1935 to May 25, 1936) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]], Hollywood CBS / Cecil B. DeMille (June 1, 1936 to January 22, 1945) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]], and Cecil B. DeMille Hollywood era (June 1, 1936 to January 22, 1945) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Charlie Forsyth (sound-effects artist on 290 recordings and performer on 2 recordings), Louis Silvers (music director on 246 recordings and music on 5 recordings), Sanford Barnett (radio adaptor on 119 recordings, director on 82 recordings, and performer on 4 recordings), Cecil B. DeMille (performer on 131 recordings, host on 36 recordings, author on 1 recording, and producer on 1 recording), George Wells (radio adaptor on 152 recordings and performer on 3 recordings), Edward Marr (performer on 140 recordings), and Melville Ruick (announcer on 139 recordings and performer on 2 recordings).

The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] (broadcast on network), [[org|org.4798d1172deaae2c|Armed Forces Radio Service]] (rebroadcast by), and [[org|org.cd82fd99edb39caa|Armed Forces Radio and Television Service]] (rebroadcast by).
Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include Romance and love relationships, Marriage, War and military conflict, Murder, Medical emergencies, and Journalism.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Network entertainment shifts toward Hollywood, Cecil B. DeMille AFRA dispute, Lux during the radio-to-television transition, and Lux branded entertainment and integrated advertising.

Programs with especially strong personnel connections in the GRH knowledge graph include [[show|screen-directors-playhouse|Screen Directors Playhouse]] (226 shared credited people), [[show|yours-truly-johnny-dollar|Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]] (149 shared credited people), [[show|escape|Escape]] (151 shared credited people), [[show|the-whistler|The Whistler]] (131 shared credited people), and [[show|nbc-university-theater|NBC University Theater]] (135 shared credited people).
